question: R152's opaque Triton norm made both MTP0 controls agree 12/12 but cost about 31% at c1 (22.6-23.0 vs 33.3 tok/s MTP0). Which cheaper implementation keeps the identity property: R153a, the same Triton kernel launched directly with fixed constants (one program per row, no wrapper), or R153b, the pure-torch decomposition left visible to Dynamo so Inductor generates one fused per-row kernel?

r153a.mechanism: custom op calling layer_norm_fwd_kernel[(M,1)] with BLOCK_N/num_warps cached per hidden size, ROWS_PER_BLOCK=1 fixed for every M

r153b.mechanism: no custom op; x.float().pow(2).mean(-1) traced and lowered by Inductor; invariance across M is the open question for this arm (static M=1 graph vs dynamic-M graph)

protocol_per_arm: same runner and gates as R152 (two MTP0 controls, two MTP1 candidates with the 100-300-token probe, MTP1 and MTP0 c1-c64 ladders); env VLLM_XPU_GEMMA_RMSNORM_TRITON=1 VLLM_XPU_RMSNORM_TRITON=1
decision_rule: an arm is adoptable only if G1-G6 pass; between adoptable arms prefer the faster MTP1 center; if neither passes G6, R152 stays the identity reference and the norm implementation is the next kernel target
amendment_after_r152: R152 MTP1 ladder: c1-c16 exact, c32 31/32, c64 61/64 (from 30/32 and 55-58/64), so the norm was one source and a smaller residual remains. Every norm in this model is the Gemma class (Qwen3NextRMSNorm is GemmaRMSNorm; the fused CUDA qk path is not used on XPU), so the remaining candidate is the FP16 head's 33+-row class (R149's chunk fix was masked by the norm). The arms therefore run as r153ah and r153bh: the a/b norm variants plus the R149 32-row head chunk (VLLM_XPU_LM_HEAD_CHUNK_ROWS=32) over the same images.
